notes:
RECONSTRUCTED FROM PHOTOS — NOT A VERIFIED NETLIST.
Function: BLE motion + heading tag. nRF52832 reads a 6-axis IMU (U8) and an HP5883 magnetometer over one I²C bus (mag 0x0D, IMU 0x6A with SDO low), wakes on IMU_INT1 / IMU_INT2 / MAG_INT, reports charge state (CHG) and battery level (VBAT_AIN, 2:1 divider), button on BTN, programmed over the 4 SWD pads.
Seen: nRF52832-QFAA SoC, USB-C (back), 3.7 V 100 mAh LiPo with its own protection board, tact switch SW2, 32 MHz crystal Y1, a second (32.768 kHz) crystal, HP5883 magnetometer (now modelled as the QMC5883P), U8 (the other IC — the LSM6DS3 IMU, as you identified), 4 SWD pads on the back, meander PCB antenna with L3 and C12, inductors L1 / L2 on the back.
Assumed: pin tie-offs of the LSM6DS3 / QMC5883P (from memory of the datasheets), charger / LDO identity, all component values, which GPIO does what, pull-ups, divider, how L1 / L2 / L3 are used. Placeholder references: U1, U2, U4, U5, J1, J2, BT1, AE1 and the unnamed resistors / capacitors.
Not modelled: U3 (pad groups at the top edge), R2/R5/R16–R18, C24 and other small parts whose function could not be read.
Antenna: ANT → [0.5 pF tuning pad] → L3 3.9 nH → C12 0.8 pF shunt → meander. Tune on a VNA with the case closed; keep metal (battery, USB shell) out of the keep-out. nRF52832 has no Coded PHY; raise TX power to +4 dBm for ≈ ×1.6 range.
Power (estimate): IMU ≈ 0.9 mA + mag ≈ 0.2 mA + nRF BLE average ≈ 0.2–0.5 mA → ≈ 1.5 mA streaming, ≈ 60 h on 100 mAh; far longer when the IMU sleeps and wakes on INT.
Verify with a meter and the datasheets before relying on any connection.

customParts.name: nRF52832-QFAA (functional)
customParts.desc: Nordic nRF52832 BLE SoC (QFN48 6×6), only the pins this board uses — marked N52832 QFAA E1 2225BZ
specs: ARM Cortex-M4F 64 MHz, BLE 5, 512 kB flash / 64 kB RAM
VDD 1.7–3.6 V (NOT directly from a 4.2 V LiPo)
32 MHz crystal on XC1/XC2, 32.768 kHz crystal on XL1/XL2
TWI on SDA/SCL, internal pull-ups available
SAADC input VBAT_AIN for the battery divider
customParts.notes: Functional symbol — pin numbers here are just the order in this list, NOT the QFN48 pin numbers. GPIO assignments (SDA, SCL, BTN, IMU_INT1/2, MAG_INT, CHG, VBAT_AIN) are assumed. Check the Nordic product specification before probing the real chip.

customParts.name: USB-C receptacle (power)
specs: 5.1 kΩ each to GND makes a sink (UFP)
customParts.notes: Seen on the back of the board at the top edge.

customParts.name: Li-ion charger SOT-23-5 (TP4054-class)
customParts.desc: Single-cell linear charger — assumed part (identity not read from the photos)
customParts.notes: ASSUMED. A 5-pin SMD IC sits next to the USB-C connector on the back; this is the usual part in that spot. Not modelled electrically in the simulation.

customParts.name: QMC5883P magnetometer (U4, marked HP5883)
customParts.desc: 3-axis magnetometer, I²C 0x2C, 16-bit, ±30 G / ±8 G. The package on the board is marked "HP 5883".
specs: on-chip — no SETC/SETP/C1 capacitors (unlike the QMC5883L)
customParts.notes: Functional pin list, not package pin numbers. Only bypass capacitors are drawn. Check the QST QMC5883P datasheet for exact pins and the INT pin behaviour.

customParts.name: LSM6DS3 (U8, 6-axis IMU)
customParts.desc: ST LSM6DS3 3-axis accelerometer + 3-axis gyroscope, I²C/SPI, LGA-14 2.5×3 mm. U8 on the board.
specs: I²C 0x6A (SA0 low) / 0x6B (SA0 high) or SPI; CS high selects I²C
SDx/SCx master port (sensor hub) — unused here
customParts.notes: Pin numbers 1–14 follow the LGA-14 order from memory of the ST datasheet — confirm against DS LSM6DS3. OCS_Aux is tied to VDDIO; SDx, SCx, SDO_Aux are left unconnected; check the datasheet for the recommended tie-offs.

customParts.name: PCB trace antenna
customParts.desc: 2.4 GHz meander antenna etched on the board edge

customParts.name: SWD test pads
customParts.desc: Four round test pads on the back: clock, data, ground, VDD
customParts.notes: Pad order read from the back-side silkscreen; confirm which pad is which with a meter.
